Dynamics3.what: Morphs between a vari-mu compressor and an expander.
Dynamics3.sound: Smooth Bezier-spline dynamics that modulates dry/wet, not just gain. Not a Fairchild clone.
Dynamics3.use: Buss and channel compression, or expansion for opening up a track.

controls.Inv/Wet: Inverted (expander side), dry, or wet blend.

Pressure6.what: A refinement of the Pressure compressor and how it moves.
Pressure6.sound: Smooth but with a more natural movement than BeziComp.
Pressure6.use: General compression on tracks and the 2-buss.

Dynamics2.what: The compressor and gate for the newer Console plugins.
Dynamics2.sound: BeziComp-style compression: fast, with no aliasing and no edges, plus a gate.

BeziComp.what: A radical compressor that eliminates aliasing.
BeziComp.sound: A curve driven by sound density: no attack or release, and sounds very clean or weird depending on settings.
BeziComp.use: Experimental, artefact-free compression. Good settings can be fussy.

Pop3.what: The dynamics section of ConsoleX: a compressor and a gate.
Pop3.sound: A full-range dynamics processor. Compression has no makeup gain, so it restrains the sound.
Pop3.use: Compression and gating on channels or the buss.

controls.Thresld: Threshold (first is the compressor, second is the gate).

Pop2.what: Pop with control and punch: attack and decay speeds plus a built-in clipper.
Pop2.sound: A crazy overcompressor with the front of sounds bursting through, now with ClipOnly2 on the output.

X2Buss.what: The updated buss processing from ConsoleX2.
X2Buss.sound: A buss EQ and one-knob compression, updated with new Bezier compression.

Pressure5.what: Pressure4 with after-boost and a built-in ClipOnly2.
Pressure5.sound: A compressor with unusual controls, built for 2-buss management and a final output.

controls.Mewines: How the ratio engages, from vari-mu to peak-retaining.

StoneFireComp.what: Some of the dynamics for ConsoleX: a Kalman multiband compressor.
StoneFireComp.sound: Two Pop3 compressors, one for the Fire (high) band and one for Stone (low).
StoneFireComp.use: Stone/Fire dynamics, from simple squash to wild effects.

controls.Attack: Attack (first is Fire, second is Stone).

Dynamics.sound: Transparent or hypersquished; the gate is triggered from the source while gating the compressed signal.
Dynamics.use: Hypercompress and gate as a unit.

Pop.what: A crazy overcompressor with a very exaggerated sound.
Pop.sound: Huge attack, bursting fronts, details jumping out, a sheer squish and gnarl.
Pop.use: Phil Collins/Genesis-style squash on drums and mixes.

DigitalBlack.sound: Tightens staccato direct-recorded tracks. Not a gentle fade gate.
DigitalBlack.use: Cleaning DI tracks and drum rooms.

Logical4.sound: Transparent and sparkly. Three stages, each bypassed when not used.

VariMu.what: A more organic variation on Pressure.
VariMu.use: When other compressors don't fit, and for organic buss compression.

ButterComp2.what: An improved ButterComp with an output control.
ButterComp2.sound: Soft, smooth, bi-polar compression, working on each half of the wave.
ButterComp2.use: Subtle, gentle compression with a cult following.

curve.what: The simplest, purest form of Recurve with no extra boosts.
curve.sound: Subtle compression with no transition point and no edges, and no gain added.
curve.use: Sitting quietly on nearly any track, balancing levels unnoticed.

Overheads.what: Compresses only part of the sound.
Overheads.sound: Drives compression from the source minus a short delay, so lows get compressed while highs slip through.
Overheads.use: Compressing drums while leaving cymbals alone.

Recurve.what: A special buss compressor with no threshold point.
Recurve.sound: Explosive and impressive: one line of code, high-resolution sine behaviour, with 6 dB of gain and a clipper.

Pyewacket.what: An old-school compressor for high-definition transients.
Pyewacket.sound: Adds no fatness, just energy and hallucinatory intensity, like Pye compressors on 60s and 70s records.
Pyewacket.use: Defining musical events on tracks and buses.

BlockParty.sound: The onset of compressing sounds is reshaped like OneCornerClip, with no lookahead. A bit distorty.

controls.Pound: How hard it limits and distorts.

SoftGate.what: A gate that mutes hiss and smooths sample tails.
SoftGate.sound: Fades the noise floor into darkness quickly or slowly.

controls.Silence: How completely it fades to silence.

Thunder.what: A compressor that keeps or exaggerates subsonic bass when you push it.
Thunder.sound: Doesn't eat low end like most compressors.
Thunder.use: Compressing bass-heavy material without losing the lows.

controls.Thunder: Amount of compression and bass behaviour.

Compresaturator.what: Fades between compressing and soft clipping.
Compresaturator.sound: A soft saturator with a springy quality; it can flutter if pushed too far.
Compresaturator.use: Stem or buss compression and loud punchy sounds.

DrumSlam.sound: Multiband tape-style distortion with its own sound. It never became a Massey TapeHead clone.

ButterComp.sound: Subtle bi-polar compression with a cult following; not an ordinary compressor.
ButterComp.use: Gentle, sweet compression for those who want exactly that.

BrassRider.what: A drum overhead rider for extreme metal mixes.
BrassRider.sound: A specialised trick for controlling overhead cymbals against sculpted spot mics.
BrassRider.use: Metal mixes with intense spot mics.

Point.sound: A mysterious, untameable plugin that works on transients.
Point.use: Making drums and transients pop or tucking them away.

controls.Point: Transient shaping, from -1 to 1. Zero is dry.

Gatelope.what: A special gate that applies filters.
Gatelope.sound: Gates a tom mic to reject cymbal bleed while lows sustain, or the opposite for kick rumble.

PodcastDeluxe.sound: Five curve-style compressors, five phase rotators and a clipper; radio-station style processing.

controls.Boost: Amount of boost into the stages.

Podcast.what: A simpler pile of curve-style compressors with hard clipping.
Podcast.sound: No latency; works as glue but doesn't pump or swell.

controls.Boost: Amount of boost into the stages.

Swell.sound: Mimics the sidechain-pumping feel by shaping attack swells.
Swell.use: Pumping swells on pads and music, without a sidechain.

PurestSquish.what: An open-sounding compressor with bass bloom.
PurestSquish.sound: Not a normal compressor: doesn't produce harmonics like analog emulations.

Pressure4.what: A compressor adjustable between vari-mu and New York peak-retaining behaviour.
Pressure4.sound: The golden-ear favourite, with a stereo linked mode inspired by diode bridges.
Pressure4.use: General compression on tracks and the 2-buss.

Surge.what: A compressor for accentuating beats and pulses.
Surge.sound: Groove-making ballistics from a compressor that responds to the rate of change.
Surge.use: Adding groove to drums and rhythmic music.

SurgeTide.what: A surge and flow dynamics plugin.
SurgeTide.sound: Three compression time constants stacked like FM waves, giving a mix that seems uncompressed but feels like tidal forces.
SurgeTide.use: Slow, deep dynamics movement on a mix.
